\chapter{Interval Greedy}
\label{ch:intervals}

\begin{tcolorbox}[enhanced, colback=white, colframe=secondaryblue, boxrule=1pt, arc=2mm]
\textbf{\large\textcolor{primaryblue}{Intervals are the classic greedy domain: choose by the earliest end, stab with the latest point, and group with the fewest machines.}}
\end{tcolorbox}

\chapterfacts{1100}{1700}{2}{4}{30}

\begin{plannedbox}[Planned Contents --- this chapter is not written yet]
\textbf{Part A --- Lessons}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, label=\textbf{A\arabic*.}, itemsep=1pt]
    \item Activity selection: earliest end first, and the stays-ahead proof
    \item Stabbing intervals with points: the latest possible point
    \item Covering requirements of several points per interval
    \item Attending events one per day: earliest deadline among the available
    \item Interval partitioning: the minimum number of groups equals the maximum overlap (sweeps are the array book)
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Part B --- Patterns} (with the two solved problems of each pattern)
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, label=\textbf{P\arabic*.}, itemsep=1pt]
    \item \textbf{Stabbing intervals with points} --- Set Intersection Size At Least Two {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 757)}, Minimum Time to Complete All Tasks {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 2589)}
    \item \textbf{Events and groups} --- Maximum Number of Events That Can Be Attended {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 1353)}, Divide Intervals Into Minimum Number of Groups {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 2406)}
\end{enumerate}
